overview.about: World Glacier Day is a United Nations observance marking the vital role of glaciers in the planet's water supply and climate, and the accelerating threat they face from warming. It anchors the UN's wider push to protect the world's frozen water reserves.
overview.nextEvent: The next World Glacier Day is marked on 21 March with events, education and campaigns worldwide. It highlights glacier monitoring and the consequences of glacier loss for rivers, sea level and communities downstream.

@graph.name: World Day for Glaciers
@graph.description: World Day for Glaciers is observed each year on 21 March, alongside World Water Day, to make the loss of the cryosphere tangible. UNESCO and the World Meteorological Organization established the observance in the International Year of Glaciers' Preservation 2025. Glaciers, snow cover and ice sheets are not remote scenery: they regulate freshwater for communities downstream, reflect sunlight and influence sea level. The day links scientific monitoring with choices that can protect mountain water systems and reduce the warming that accelerates ice loss. A useful way to follow it is to look beyond a single photograph of retreating ice and ask what changes in seasonal meltwater mean for the people, rivers and ecosystems below each glacier.

exploreIntro: These places are shown because their landscapes make glaciers visible: Iceland has ice caps and volcanic glaciers, Switzerland has Alpine glaciers, and Canada connects mountain ice with Arctic-scale change.
participationIntro: Use the day to connect glacier loss with practical climate awareness:

participationSteps.text: Read or share a clear glacier-loss explainer from a trusted climate or science source.
Use the day in a class, workplace note or community post to explain why glaciers matter for water, sea level and mountain regions.
Support a local climate, mountain, water or science-education activity if one is available.
Avoid turning the day into generic nature content; keep the focus on glaciers, ice and climate impacts.
